title: Revealing cumulative dispersion in non-uniform feature waveguides: From local k-ω relations to global spectra and dispersion-compensated localisation.
abstract: Non-uniform feature waveguides, whose cross-section varies along the propagation axis, host feature-guided wave (FGW) modes confined to structural features such as bends, welds, and stiffeners in plate-like structures. Although FGWs in uniform features have been extensively studied, their non-uniform counterparts have not been reported. For one-dimensionally varying cross-sections, such as thickness-varying plates, guided waves' dispersion is governed primarily by the local thickness and can often be described through frequency-thickness equivalence. For two-dimensionally varying cross-sections, such as non-uniform bends, cross-sectional variation cannot be characterised by a single scalar; the irregular 2D profile modifies wave-energy confinement and modal existence. Using non-uniform bends as a demonstration, we develop a local-to-global framework applicable to slowly varying non-uniform waveguide, whether open or closed. At the local scale, SAFE-PML eigen-analysis of frozen cross-sections yields position-dependent dispersion relations (local k-ω relations); at the global scale, 2D-FFT of the propagating wavefield produces a cumulative frequency-wavenumber spectrum that represents the superposition of all local k-ω contributions along the propagation path-the key measurable manifestation of cumulative dispersion. This spectral interpretation enables two complementary defect assessment functionalities. Defect detection is achieved through excess-bandwidth analysis: the geometric variation of the intact waveguide defines a reference bandwidth, whereas defect-induced scattering redistributes spectral energy into out-of-band components, providing global damage indicators. Defect localisation is accomplished by path-dependent dispersion compensation, in which the position-dependent local wavenumbers obtained from the frozen-cross-section SAFE-PML analysis are accumulated along each source-candidate-receiver path to compensate the phase of the defect-scattered wavefield. The proposed framework is validated through three-dimensional finite-element (FE) simulations and experimental measurements on representative non-uniform feature waveguides.
